name: BIOMEDICAL WASTE AUTOCLAVE
desc: The INNOLAB INSTRUMENTS INNO-BWA-220 Biomedical Waste Autoclave is an industrial-grade, high-capacity steam sterilization system engineered for the safe and complete decontamination of medical and bio-hazardous waste. The advanced fully automatic models feature a robust triple-walled construction comprising a Stainless Steel 304/316L sterilization chamber.
principle: The INNOLAB INSTRUMENTS BIOMEDICAL WASTE AUTOCLAVE operates on the principle of saturated steam sterilization under elevated pressure, utilizing a triple-walled stainless steel chamber and jacket to achieve uniform temperatures of 121°C to 134°C at pressures of 15 to 30 psi. This thermal process irreversibly denatures microbial proteins, nucleic acids, and enzymes, ensuring complete inactivation of vegetative bacteria, viruses, fungi, and highly resistant bacterial endospores such as Bacillus stearothermophilus and Geobacillus stearothermophilus, which serve as biological indicators for sterilization efficacy. The system incorporates pre-vacuum and post-vacuum cycles via a water ring vacuum pump to remove air pockets and enhance steam penetration into porous loads, while a 0.2µ fresh air inlet filter prevents recontamination during cooling. Designed for biomedical waste decontamination, it is essential for hospitals, diagnostic laboratories, research institutes, and pharmaceutical facilities to safely treat infectious sharps, cultures, pathological waste, blood products, and other bio-hazardous materials in compliance with WHO guidelines, ISO 17665, and national biomedical waste management rules. The PLC-based HMI touch screen controller with data monitoring and recording enables validated cycles, Bowie-Dick and leak tests, and automatic water filling, ensuring reproducible sterilization for B.Sc/M.Sc students, PhD researchers, and clinical staff handling strong disinfectants, cytotoxic drugs, and genetically modified organisms.
sop: Ensure the autoclave is connected to power, water supply, and compressed air (if applicable), and that the chamber is empty and clean.
Load the biomedical waste bags or containers into the sterilization chamber, ensuring not to overfill and allowing steam circulation.
Close and lock the radial locking door securely.
Press the 'SET' button once on the PID controller to enter parameter setting mode.
Use the 'UP' and 'DOWN' arrows to adjust the target sterilization temperature (e.g., 121°C or 134°C) as required for the waste type.
Press 'SET' again to lock the temperature value, then press 'SET' once more to set the sterilization hold time (e.g., 15-30 minutes) using the 'UP' and 'DOWN' arrows, and press 'SET' to confirm.
Select the appropriate cycle (pre-vacuum, gravity, or test cycle) on the HMI touch screen, and start the cycle.
Monitor the cycle progress on the display, ensuring pressure and temperature reach set points and remain stable during the holding phase.
After cycle completion, allow the chamber to cool and pressure to drop to atmospheric level before opening the door.
Carefully unload the sterilized waste using heat-resistant gloves, and transfer to designated disposal containers.
Perform daily maintenance: check water level, clean chamber, and run a Bowie-Dick test if required.

Safety Warning: Never open the door while the chamber is pressurized or hot; always verify that the pressure gauge reads zero and the temperature is below 80°C before unlocking, and wear appropriate PPE (heat-resistant gloves, face shield, lab coat) to prevent steam burns or exposure to residual biohazards.
features: Triple Walled construction with Stainless Steel 304 / 316L chamber and boiler
PLC Based HMI Color Touch Screen Controller with Data Monitoring & Recording
Pre and Post Vacuum Cycles driven by a Water Ring Vacuum Pump
0.2µ Fresh Air Inlet Filter for safe air purification
Comprehensive safeties including Over Pressure Safety and Emergency Stop
